source_review.notes: Checked all twelve structured primary references. Current Kubernetes documentation supports Deployment/ReplicaSet revision behavior, rolling versus recreate strategies, maxSurge/maxUnavailable rounding, minReadySeconds, progress conditions/deadlines, pause/resume, revision-history limits, lifecycle, and disruption boundaries; importantly, a progress deadline reports rather than automatically rolls back. Gateway API documentation supports proportional backend weights and progressive traffic splitting. Current Argo Rollouts documentation supports canary/blue-green strategies, analysis outcomes, abort behavior, preview/active routing, and bounded rollback windows. OpenGitOps provides declarative/versioned/reconciled principles, while SLSA v1.2 and Sigstore policy-controller documentation support consumer-side artifact/provenance and admission verification.

Checked tuples, time functions, conjunction, equality, nonnegative constraints, ratios, revision symbols, and state functions with repository-compatible GitHub math delimiters.

proof_review.notes: The chapter states no theorem and contains no deductive proof; the assurance chain is explicitly conditional on controllers, routing, telemetry, compatibility, and policy assumptions.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No proof sketch is claimed; artifact, environment, controller, router, telemetry, statistical, dependency, human, schema, and recovery limitations are stated.

Worked rollout, traffic, telemetry, migration, GitOps, regional, and recovery cases are framed as scenarios rather than observed incidents.
Protocol/controller documentation, platform recommendations, mathematical models, and operational metrics to collect remain distinguishable.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external deployment, production canary, statistical experiment, migration, rollback, regional release, security assessment, or incident is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently separates build, release, deployment, reconciliation, rollout, traffic, analysis, promotion, user outcome, and recovery while binding exact artifacts, configuration, targets, strategy, evidence, and compatibility.

practitioner_review.notes: A practitioner can define candidates and state machines, separate authority, verify artifacts/targets, run preflight, choose rollout strategies, control/observe traffic, design gates, coordinate configuration/data/clients, select recovery, reconcile declaratively, progress regions, and record outcomes.

pedagogical_review.notes: The sequence moves from candidate/API/authority through verification, preflight, rollout strategies, native behavior, traffic, analysis, configuration/data compatibility, recovery, GitOps, regions, records, and measurement. Ten examples cover digest identity, rolling arithmetic, business outcomes, routing realization, missing telemetry, schema rollback, shared dependencies, field ownership, regional compatibility, and recovery windows. Five exercises progress from definitions through lifecycle tracing, diagnosis, rollout design, and ambiguous incident transfer, with complete model answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
